description: Media Arts Year 1-2 width tiers — 5 standards, all capability strands. Generated from width_generation_prompt.md v1.0.
subject: Media Arts

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term — one media task type, one technology, or one production context.
width_notes.typical_width: Full Y1-2 scope from common elaboration cases — multiple media types encountered, representations constructed with intention, responsible use principles applied.
width_notes.wider: Additional task contexts: different media forms, different audiences, different production tools, First Nations media arts contexts where elaborations indicate them.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. Variants of the same activity merged. First Nations elaborations always represented in wider.

AC9AMA2C01.minimum_width: Use at least one media technology (camera, recording device, or drawing/animation tool) to construct a representation — a short image sequence, captioned images, or simple animation — that communicates a recognisable story or idea.
AC9AMA2C01.typical_width: Construct representations using a range of media languages and technologies (images, sound, text, animation); apply basic shot types and composition decisions; sequence media elements to create meaning for an audience; make deliberate choices about what to include, delete or modify.
wider: Create an advertisement or promotional media work for a specific purpose (e.g. recommending appropriate camera behaviour), applying shot type decisions (long, mid, close-up) and reflecting on how the choice of shot communicates meaning to the audience
Construct a comic book or captioned image sequence that retells a familiar or traditional story, using Viewpoints questions to make composition decisions
Explore claymation or stop-motion animation by creating a character using images, sounds and/or movement — reflecting on how composition choices affect meaning
elaborations: creating a story through a series of captioned or voice-over images or direct to camera footage; exploring composition through character creation using images, sounds, and/or animation; for example, claymation
selecting and editing images, sound and text to re-create the characters in well-known stories or songs, using Viewpoints to develop questions when making decisions about composition
capturing and sequencing images and text to create a media arts work, such as a comic book that retells familiar or traditional stories
producing and presenting a media arts work for a particular purpose; for example, creating an advertisement that recommends appropriate behaviour when using cameras
using features such as shot types in media arts works; for example, identifying long-shots, mid-shots and close-ups; discussing what the shots tell the audience about the story

AC9AMA2D01.minimum_width: Experiment with one digital tool (e.g. camera, recording device, or image editing app) to capture or manipulate media elements — discovering at least one way the tool changes how an idea or story is communicated.
AC9AMA2D01.typical_width: Explore multiple ways digital tools can capture and manipulate images, sound and text; experiment with how different choices (close vs distant shots, different sound effects, different text headings) change meaning; use Viewpoints questions to guide experimentation and reflection.
wider: Explore how sound communicates ideas by creating sound effects using found objects or recording technology, integrating them with a picture book or image sequence — experimenting with what changes when sound is added, removed or modified

Experiment with combining text, symbols and images to communicate ideas or emotions — for example, creating headlines with digital images to change or reinforce meaning, and discussing how the combination creates different audience responses
Investigate how moving further from or closer to a subject changes the meaning of a captured image — applying Viewpoints questions systematically to a series of distance experiments
elaborations: exploring ways to use digital tools to capture moving image; for example, using a digital device to capture and manipulate short videos, add sound effects or voice-overs, and considering how best to combine the visual and audio elements to communicate ideas or a narrative
exploring how sound can be used to communicate ideas; for example, creating sound effects using found objects or sound recording technology to integrate with a picture book story
experimenting with images; for example, retelling the story of a school day using a digital camera to capture still or moving images and adding appropriate captions

experimenting with ways that media artists communicate with audiences by combining text, symbols and images; for example, combining headlines, subtitles and digital images to communicate ideas or emotions

using Viewpoints to develop questions as they experiment with media technologies, such as, "What happens if I take a photo up close to the object, and how does it change as I move further away?", "How can I change the meaning of this image by adding different text headings?"

AC9AMA2E01.minimum_width: Identify at least one type of media arts work from their own life or community and explain what story or knowledge it communicates and who made it.
AC9AMA2E01.typical_width: Explore a range of media arts works from different cultural contexts and communities; discuss why and how media arts works communicate cultural knowledge; consider the roles of media artists and what permissions mean; engage with media arts works across different types (podcasts, animations, news bulletins, advertisements).
wider: Explore media arts works created by First Nations Australians (e.g. podcasts, animated children's shows) to investigate when, where, how and why they share cultural knowledge — using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australian communities

Investigate how media arts works in different community contexts (national celebrations, cultural events, NAIDOC Week) communicate cultural knowledge and identity — discussing the purpose and audience of each

Compare media arts works from different cultures (e.g. how children's animation looks and sounds differently across countries) and discuss what these differences suggest about cultural values and storytelling traditions
elaborations: identifying where they might experience media arts works in their lives and communities; for example, considering how media arts works communicate cultural knowledge and the purpose of a range of media types

using Viewpoints to ask questions about societies and cultures; for example, "What story is this media arts work telling me/us?", "Who made this media arts work?", "Where is this media arts work from?"
discussing the roles of media artists and what permission means; for example, deciding on a class set of rules for using and creating images, sounds and text in media arts works
considering how media arts works communicate and celebrate cultural knowledge in their own communities; for example, through podcasts or animated children's shows

AC9AMA2E02.minimum_width: Explore one media arts work created by First Nations Australians and identify how it communicates cultural knowledge — describing at least one visual, audio, or interactive element used.
AC9AMA2E02.typical_width: Explore a range of media arts works created and/or co-created by First Nations Australians across different forms (television programs, cartoons/animations, print media, advertisements); identify how visual, audio and/or interactive elements are used; discuss when and why these works are created and shared; engage with community representatives or accredited resources.
wider: Explore First Nations Australian media arts works created for significant occasions (NAIDOC Week, National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children's Day, Sorry Day, Reconciliation Week) and discuss how the work communicates cultural knowledge relevant to the occasion

Investigate how colours, symbols and patterns are used in First Nations Australian media arts works — working with community representatives or accredited resources to understand their cultural significance
Explore media arts works created by First Nations Australians that communicate cultural narratives, and compare how the same narrative is told using different media forms
elaborations: exploring when, where, how and why First Nations Australians use media arts works to share knowledge about their cultures; for example, during celebrations such as National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children's Day, NAIDOC Week, Reconciliation Week or the acknowledgement of significant occasions including Sorry Day

exploring children's television programs, cartoons/animations and child-focused print media, such as an advertisement encouraging people to adopt a healthy lifestyle, created and distributed by First Nations Australians

observing how visual, audio and/or interactive elements are used in media arts works created by First Nations Australians; for example, exploring colours, symbols and patterns used in media arts works with representatives of the First Nations Australian community or through resources that are created or co-created by First Nations Australians
exploring media arts works created and/or co-created by First Nations Australians that communicate cultural narratives

AC9AMA2P01.minimum_width: Present a media arts work to a small audience (class, small group, or teacher) and explain how it was made and what they enjoyed about making it.
AC9AMA2P01.typical_width: Share media arts works in informal settings (class, another class, school intranet); apply relevant permission and protocol considerations when sharing images or cultural material; consider audience relationships when creating, rehearsing and presenting; engage with audience responses.
wider: Collect and share class stories as a class news bulletin, applying permission protocols (obtaining permission from individuals and respecting any cultural material belonging to a collective group)
Create, rehearse and record a radio play in a small group — seeking permission to share with another class, and reflecting on what it felt like to have a real audience

Consult relevant people or online safety resources to develop a class set of rules for using and creating images, sounds and text in media arts works — presenting the rules to the class and explaining the reasoning behind each
elaborations: collecting and sharing class stories and presenting them in the form of a class news bulletin, with permission of the people involved and observing relevant protocols
presenting a media arts work they have made to the class, a small group or their teacher, and explaining how they made it and what they enjoyed about making it
considering relationships that peers may have with their work when creating, rehearsing and recording a radio play, and seeking permission to share it with another class

exploring what permission means; for example, consulting relevant people such as cultural knowledge holders or using online safety resources, and deciding on a class set of rules for using and creating images, sounds and text in media arts works
